questions.question: Who discovered the Bharhut stupa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alexander Cunningham**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Alexander Cunningham**, regarded as the "Father of Indian Archaeology," discovered the Bharhut Stupa in **1873**.
 
• He extensively documented the stupa's remains, including its intricate sculptures and inscriptions, which are valuable for understanding early Buddhist art and architecture.
 
• The Bharhut Stupa, located in present-day **Madhya Pradesh**, dates back to the **2nd century BCE**, showcasing early Buddhist relief carvings and inscriptions in the Brahmi script.
 
• Cunningham's discovery provided critical insights into the cultural and religious practices of the **Mauryan and Sunga periods**.
 
• His findings on Bharhut are recorded in his archaeological reports, which remain foundational for the study of ancient Indian history and early Buddhist art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharhut Stupa**

 
 
• The Bharhut Stupa is an ancient Buddhist monument known for its remarkable railings and gateways adorned with narrative relief sculptures.
 
• Its carvings depict **Jataka tales** (stories of the Buddha’s previous lives) and other Buddhist symbols.
 
• It was originally commissioned during the **Mauryan Empire** and later renovated during the **Sunga dynasty**.
 
• Many artifacts from Bharhut, including reliefs and inscriptions, are now preserved in the **Indian Museum in Kolkata**.
 
 
 
• **Alexander Cunningham**
 
 
• Alexander Cunningham was the first **Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**, founded in 1861.
 
• He conducted pioneering archaeological explorations of major sites like **Sarnath, Taxila, and Bodh Gaya**.
 
• His systematic documentation and study of inscriptions helped reconstruct India’s ancient history and timeline.
 
• Cunningham's work laid the foundation for modern archaeology in India.
 
 
 
• **Buddhist Art and Architecture**
 
 
• The Bharhut Stupa is an example of **early Buddhist art**, characterized by narrative reliefs and symbolic depictions of Buddhist themes.
 
• Unlike later Buddhist monuments, early art like Bharhut avoided anthropomorphic representations of the Buddha, instead using symbols like the **lotus and wheel**.
 
• The railings and gateways of Bharhut illustrate the transition to more elaborate decorative elements seen in later sites like **Sanchi**.
 
• Inscriptions at Bharhut provide valuable evidence of early Buddhist practices, patronage, and the use of the **Brahmi script**.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**
 
 
• The ASI, established in 1861, is responsible for preserving and documenting India’s cultural heritage.
 
• It conducts excavations, research, and conservation of historical monuments and archaeological sites.
 
• Under Cunningham’s leadership, the ASI began systematic archaeological surveys and excavations in India.
 
• The efforts of the ASI have been instrumental in understanding India’s ancient civilization and its contributions to global heritage.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question:
Which of the given statements is correct?

I. When Alivardi Khan died in 1756, Siraj-ud-daulah became the nawab of Bengal.

II. In 1757, Robert Clive led the company’s army against Siraj-ud-daulah at Plassey.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At least **80 years old, Alivardi Khan **passed away from dropsy on **April 9, 1756, at 5 am.**
 
• **Siraj-ud-Daula**, his daughter's son, who was** 23** at the time, succeeded him.
 
• He was **Bengal's final Nawab** to rule on his own.
 
• The** East India Company **began to dominate over** Bengal **at the conclusion of his era.
 
• Siraj was enraged by the widespread abuse of** trade privileges by EIC authorities.**
 
• The** battle of Plassey in 1757 **was brought on by EIC's continued **wrongdoing **against Siraj-Ud-Daulah.
 
• On **June 23, 1757,** the Battle of Plassey took place in northeastern India.
 
• **Robert Clive's British East India Company **soldiers confronted Siraj-ud-Daulah, the last Nawab of Bengal, and his French allies.
 
• The head of Nawab's army,** Mir Jafar, **was bought off by Robert Clive with the promise of becoming the** Nawab of Bengal.**
 
• In **1757, Siraj-ud-Daulah **was beaten by **Clive at Plassey**, and **Calcutta **was taken.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Robert Clive:

 
 
• The** Bengal Presidency's first British governor** was Robert Clive.
 
• Clive is usually regarded as having laid the groundwork fo**r Bengali British East India Company** dominance.
 
• **Corruption** was rife during his** first term as governor of Bengal,** under Nawab Mir Jaffar.
 
• The business's only goal was to **maximize profits** at the expense of the** peasants.**
 
• In India, he accumulated a **sizable personal fortune** before departing for** London in 1760.**
 
• As **Bengal's Governor and Commander-in-Chie**f, he returned to India in 1765.
 
• In 1765, he founded a** "Society of Commerce**," but it was eventually disbanded.
 
• Bengal's king was now **Mir Qasim, the son-in-law **of Mir Jaffar.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: Under which of the following Acts, was Warren Hastings appointed as the Governor-General of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Regulating Act, 1773**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Regulating Act, 1773 was the first act passed by the British Parliament to control the administration of the East India Company in India.
 
• It marked the beginning of parliamentary oversight and introduced significant administrative reforms in the governance of the company.
 
• The Act designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal, with Warren Hastings being the first to hold this position.
 
• The Governor-General was given authority over the presidencies of Madras and Bombay, establishing a centralized administrative structure.
 
• A Supreme Court was also established in Calcutta (now Kolkata) as part of the act to administer justice according to British law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Government of India Act, 1858**

 
 
• This act marked the end of the East India Company's rule and the beginning of direct control by the British Crown.
 
• It transferred the administration of India to the British monarchy, establishing the office of the Secretary of State for India.
 
• The act aimed to improve governance and centralize authority under the British government.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act, 1909**
 
 
• Also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, this act introduced significant changes in the Indian legislative structure.
 
• It expanded the legislative councils at both central and provincial levels and allowed for greater Indian representation.
 
• The act introduced separate electorates for Muslims, a significant development in Indian political history.
 
 
 
• **The Government of India Act, 1935**
 
 
• This was the longest act passed by the British Parliament concerning the governance of India.
 
• It proposed the establishment of a federal structure in India, including the creation of provinces and princely states.
 
• The act introduced provincial autonomy and expanded the electorate significantly.
 
• It laid the foundation for the eventual independence and partition of India in 1947.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: Who among the following signed the Treaty of Allahabad in August 1765 with the Nawab of Awadh and Shah Alam II, the Mughal Emperor?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Robert Clive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Robert Clive**, also known as **Clive of India**, was an important figure in the establishment of British control in India.
 
• He signed the **Treaty of Allahabad** in **August 1765** with the **Nawab of Awadh** and **Shah Alam II**, the Mughal Emperor.
 
• The treaty was a result of the **Battle of Buxar** (1764), where the British East India Company defeated the combined forces of the Nawab of Awadh, the Mughal Emperor, and Mir Qasim, the Nawab of Bengal.
 
• The treaty granted the East India Company **Diwani rights** (revenue collection) over **Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa**, which marked the beginning of British fiscal dominance in India.
 
• Under the treaty, the **Nawab of Awadh** had to pay a large indemnity to the Company and surrender territories in return for British protection.
 
• **Shah Alam II**, the Mughal Emperor, was given an annual pension, effectively making him a dependent on the East India Company.
 
• The treaty was a significant milestone in British imperial expansion and the consolidation of their rule in India.
 
• **Robert Clive** played a central role in shaping the administrative and political structure of British India during this period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Earl Mountbatten**__

 __
 
• **Earl Mountbatten of Burma** was the last **Viceroy of India** and the first **Governor-General of independent India**.
 
• He oversaw the **partition of India** in 1947 and the transfer of power from the British to Indian leaders.
 
• He is not associated with events like the **Treaty of Allahabad**, which occurred much earlier in the 18th century.
 
 
 
• **William Bentinck**__
 __
 
• **William Bentinck** served as the **Governor-General of India** from 1828 to 1835.
 
• He is known for his **social reforms**, such as the abolition of **Sati** and promoting **Western education**.
 
• Bentinck’s tenure was in the 19th century, long after the **Treaty of Allahabad** was signed.
 
 
 
• **Warren Hastings**__
 
 
• **Warren Hastings** was the first **Governor-General of India** (1773–1785).
 
• He is known for his administrative reforms and efforts to consolidate British control in India.
 
• Although Hastings played a significant role in Indian history, the **Treaty of Allahabad** predates his tenure as Governor-General.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: The East India Company lost all its administrative powers with the enforcement of __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Government of India Act, 1858**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Government of India Act, 1858** marked the end of the East India Company's rule in India.
 
• Following the Revolt of 1857, the Act transferred administrative powers from the East India Company to the **British Crown**.
 
• This Act established the office of the **Secretary of State for India**, who was responsible for overseeing Indian administration from Britain.
 
• A **15-member Council of India** was formed to assist the Secretary of State in managing Indian affairs.
 
• The Governor-General of India was re-designated as the **Viceroy of India**, representing the Crown in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Regulating Act, 1773**

 
 
• The first attempt by the British government to regulate the East India Company's affairs in India.
 
• Established the office of the Governor-General of Bengal (later Governor-General of India).
 
• Set up a Supreme Court in Calcutta to oversee legal matters.
 
 
 
• **The Charter Act of 1853**
 
 
• Last Charter Act granted to the East India Company by the British Parliament.
 
• Ended the Company's trade monopoly in India and allowed open competition.
 
• Introduced the concept of a competitive examination for recruitment into the Indian Civil Service (ICS).
 
 
 
• **The Indian Councils Act, 1892**
 
 
• Provided for the expansion of legislative councils in British India.
 
• Allowed limited participation of Indians in legislative processes through indirect elections.
 
• Marked the beginning of Indian representation in governance.
 
 
 
• **The Revolt of 1857**
 
 
• Also known as the First War of Indian Independence or Sepoy Mutiny.
 
• Triggered by various economic, political, and social grievances against the British administration.
 
• Its failure led to significant administrative reforms, including the enactment of the Government of India Act, 1858.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: In which of the following systems was the charge of collecting the revenue and paying it to the Company given to the village headman, rather than the zamindar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahalwari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mahalwari system was a land revenue system implemented in British India.
 
• Under this system, the village headman, known as the 'lambardar,' was responsible for collecting revenue from the villagers.
 
• The revenue collected by the lambardar was then paid to the British East India Company.
 
• This system was introduced by Holt Mackenzie in 1822 and later modified by Lord William Bentinck in 1833.
 
• The Mahalwari system was primarily implemented in the North-Western Provinces, parts of Central India, and Punjab.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zamindari System**

 
 
• Also known as the Permanent Settlement System, it was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793.
 
• Under this system, zamindars were recognized as the landowners and were responsible for collecting and paying revenue to the Company.
 
• The zamindars were granted hereditary rights over the land and were supposed to pay a fixed amount of revenue annually.
 
• This system was primarily implemented in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
 
 
 
• **Ryotwari System**
 
 
• This system was introduced by Thomas Munro in 1820.
 
• Under the Ryotwari system, the individual cultivator or ryot was recognized as the landowner.
 
• The ryots were directly responsible for paying the land revenue to the British government.
 
• This system was primarily implemented in Madras, Bombay, parts of Assam, and Coorg provinces.
 
 
 
• **Iqtadari System**
 
 
• The Iqtadari system was introduced during the Delhi Sultanate period.
 
• Under this system, the land was divided into Iqtas, and the responsibility of collecting revenue was given to the Iqtadars.
 
• The Iqtadars were responsible for maintaining law and order and providing military assistance to the Sultan.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT?

A) 1833 Charter Act has changed the designation for Governor-General of Bengal, renamed as Governor-General of India.

B) Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor General of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Neither A nor B**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **1833 Charter Act** was a significant legislation passed by the British Parliament aimed at reforming the administration of India.
 
• This act did **rename the Governor-General of Bengal** to the **Governor-General of India**, granting him authority over all British territories in India. However, it did not make sweeping administrative changes in his powers as implied in statement A.
 
• While the title of **Governor-General of India** was introduced, the act also centralized the power structure, bringing all provinces under the direct control of the Governor-General.
 
• **Lord William Bentinck** is widely regarded as the first Governor-General of India in terms of the title, but technically his designation was still Governor-General of Bengal under the earlier framework.
 
• The title of Governor-General of India was effectively formalized for the first time with **Lord Charles Metcalfe** serving as acting Governor-General after Bentinck, followed by Lord Auckland.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Charter Act of 1833**__

 __
 
• The Charter Act of 1833 is also known as the **Government of India Act 1833**.
 
• It was the last of the series of Charter Acts passed by the British Parliament between **1793 and 1833**.
 
• The act aimed at centralizing the administration of British India by creating a unitary government under the Governor-General of India.
 
• It vested legislative power exclusively in the hands of the Governor-General in Council.
 
• The act also opened the doors for Indians to be employed in the British administration, although this was not implemented effectively.
 
 
 
• **Lord William Bentinck**__
 
 
• He served as the **Governor-General of Bengal** from **1828 to 1835**.
 
• He is known for his significant reforms in **social, economic, and educational spheres**.
 
• Bentinck is credited with abolishing the practice of **Sati** and suppressing the **Thuggee cult**.
 
• He also introduced **English as the medium of instruction** in Indian education as per Macaulay’s recommendations.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: Which act was passed by the British Parliament to control the territories of the East India Company majorly in Bengal in the year 1773?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Regulating Act.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Regulating Act:-**

 
 
• The Regulating Act was passed by the British Parliament in 1773.
 
• **The Act was designed to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India and to curb its powers.**
 
• It was the first major intervention by the British government in the affairs of the East India Company and paved the way for further reforms and acts.
 
• The Act established a system of governance in India, with a Governor-General and a Supreme Council, and also introduced other reforms such as the establishment of a court of justice in Calcutta.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Government of India Act:-**

 
 
• The Government of India Act is a set of laws passed by the British Parliament between 1773 and 1935 to regulate the government of India.
 
• **The Government of India Act 1935 was a landmark piece of legislation that introduced a number of important constitutional reforms in India, including:**
 
 
• The establishment of a federal system of government, with a central government and provincial governments.
 
• The introduction of direct elections to the provincial legislatures.
 
• The expansion of the franchise to include more Indians.
 
• The creation of a Federal Court, with the power to adjudicate on disputes between the central government and the provincial governments.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act:-**
 
 
• The Indian Councils Act was a series of laws passed by the British Parliament between 1861 and 1909 to expand the size and functions of the legislative councils in British India.
 
• **These acts were introduced in response to growing demands for self-government from Indian nationalists.**
 
 
 
• **Charter Act:-**
 
 
• A Charter Act is a law passed by the British Parliament to renew the charter of the British East India Company, which was a private company that ruled British India on behalf of the British Crown.
 
• **The Charter Acts were passed every 20 years, and they regulated the company's trade and administrative powers.**

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: Who among the following Indian leaders was the first member to be elected to the British Parliament?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji** was the first Indian to be elected as a **member of the British Parliament**.
 
• He was elected in the year **1892** from the constituency of **Finsbury Central, London**, representing the **Liberal Party**.
 
• Known as the **Grand Old Man of India**, he played a pivotal role in **advocating for Indian rights and self-rule** during the colonial era.
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji was a key figure in the **Indian National Congress** and served as its president three times—in **1886, 1893, and 1906**.
 
• He is renowned for articulating the concept of the **Drain of Wealth**, which highlighted the economic exploitation of India by the British.
 
• His seminal work, **Poverty and Un-British Rule in India**, is a critical document that lays out the systematic drain of resources from India to Britain.
 
• Naoroji's election to the British Parliament was a significant achievement that brought Indian issues to the forefront of British politics.
 
• He actively campaigned for **Indian representation**, economic justice, and the end of discriminatory policies in British governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Motilal Nehru**__

 __
 
• Motilal Nehru was a prominent **Indian freedom fighter** and politician.
 
• He was one of the key leaders of the **Indian National Congress** and served as its president twice—in **1919 and 1928**.
 
• He was known for his involvement in the **Swaraj Party**, which aimed to achieve self-rule within the British framework.
 
• Motilal Nehru was the father of **Jawaharlal Nehru**, India's first Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Bhikaji Cama**__
 __
 
• Bhikaji Cama was a prominent **Indian revolutionary** and a key figure in the Indian independence movement.
 
• She is widely remembered for unfurling the first version of the **Indian national flag** at an international socialist conference in **Stuttgart, Germany, in 1907**.
 
• Bhikaji Cama worked extensively to promote India's cause on an international platform and is regarded as a pioneer of Indian nationalism abroad.
 
 
 
• **Lala Hardayal**__
 
 
• Lala Hardayal was a noted **Indian nationalist, freedom fighter, and intellectual.**
 
• He was one of the founders of the **Ghadar Party**, which aimed to overthrow British rule in India.
 
• Hardayal was a brilliant scholar who earned degrees from **Oxford University** and worked to unite Indians living abroad for the cause of independence.
 
• He contributed significantly to revolutionary movements and was known for his writings and speeches advocating for freedom.
